title: refactor(spec)!: retire three orphan operator vocabularies (objectui#2945 Track A)
body:
Track A of objectstack-ai/objectui#2945 — the one track of that issue that is safe to land today. Three operator vocabularies with **no importer at all**, each contradicting the vocabulary that is actually enforced.

Zero-consumer verified by grep across framework `packages/` + `apps/`, objectui, and cloud, on this branch's merge base (not read from the audit).

## `AggregationFunctionEnum` — `shared/enums.zod.ts`

Its own doc comment claimed it was *"used across query, data-engine, analytics, field"*. It was used by nothing.

`AggregationFunction` (`data/query.zod.ts`) is what the query engine, `service-analytics`' dataset compiler and the native-SQL strategy all gate on — and the two disagreed:

| | members |
|---|---|
| `AggregationFunctionEnum` (removed) | count, sum, avg, min, max, count_distinct, **percentile, median, stddev, variance** |
| `AggregationFunction` (kept) | count, sum, avg, min, max, count_distinct, **array_agg, string_agg** |

It also exported a **type** named `AggregationFunction` while `data/query.zod.ts` exports a **value** of that name — the same identifier in two declaration spaces with different members, which is a trap waiting for whoever first writes `z.infer<typeof AggregationFunction>` next to a bare `AggregationFunction` annotation.

## `FilterOperator` — `api/websocket.zod.ts`

`FilterOperator` fed `EventFilterCondition` → `EventFilterSchema` → `EventSubscriptionSchema.filters`. The whole subtree is removed, `filters` included.

No runtime ever evaluated an event filter: `matchesSubscription` matches on object name and event type only (`contracts/realtime-service.ts`), and the subscription shape the transports actually carry is the separate, deliberately unvalidated `filters: z.unknown()` on `SubscriptionEventSchema` (`api/realtime.zod.ts`).

So this was a *second* modelling of event filtering, disagreeing with both the live one and with `VALID_AST_OPERATORS`, that advertised a capability no code provided — **a subscriber who set `filters` would have received every event.** Removed rather than wired up: the surface that matters is the realtime contract, and it should grow one filter vocabulary rather than inherit an orphan's.

## `ODataFilterOperatorSchema` — `api/odata.zod.ts`

Nothing parses an OData `$filter` against it. `$filter` is carried as an opaque string (`ODataQuerySchema.$filter`, and the `odata` adapter template in `query-adapter.zod.ts` — which only `@see`s this file, it does not import it). An enum mixing operators with `(` and `)` could not validate an expression anyway: it describes tokens, not a grammar.

A real OData implementation needs a parser, and that parser should lower onto `AST_OPERATOR_MAP` (`data/filter.zod.ts`) like every other entry point. Kept as an enum, this was only a way for the count of filter vocabularies to grow.

`ODataFilterFunctionSchema` (contains/startswith/tolower/…) is an adjacent orphan, left in place: it is a *function* vocabulary, not an operator one, and out of scope here.

## Why this is `major`, and why it is still safe

All three were reachable as public exports (`@objectstack/spec/shared`, `@objectstack/spec/api`), so removing them is breaking and the changeset is `major` — it lands in the 17.0.0 that is already accumulating majors in `pre` mode.

Nothing is **narrowed**. No accepted value stops being accepted, so no already-stored metadata and no in-flight payload changes meaning. That distinction is the whole point of objectui#2945: narrowing `VALID_AST_OPERATORS` turns a working bare-triple filter into a silently unfiltered query (#3948), and retiring a `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS` alias orphans live `sys_metadata` rows, because `saveMeta` persists the authored body verbatim. Both remain blocked. Deleting an orphan is not in that class.

In-file comments record what was removed and why at each of the three sites, so the next audit finds the reasoning instead of re-deriving it.

## Verification

- Full `@objectstack/spec` suite: **6917 tests across 266 files, all pass**.
- `tsc --noEmit` on `packages/spec`: clean.
- Affected suites specifically (`websocket`, `odata`, `shared/enums`): 122 pass.

Refs objectstack-ai/objectui#2945, objectstack-ai/objectui#2901, #3948
